added.description:
Job Summary

Are you passionate about creating safer workplaces while making a meaningful impact on manufacturing operations?

IFF is a global leader in flavors, fragrances, food ingredients and health & biosciences. We deliver sustainable innovations that elevate everyday products.

Global Operations:
Ensuring excellence in execution—from procurement to supply chain and reliability—delivering quality, safety, efficiency and sustainability across the value chain.

The Environmental Health & Safety Specialist
role is based in Memphis, Tennessee (onsite role)
.

This position serves as the site's primary resource for environmental compliance, permitting, regulatory reporting, and environmental risk management while also supporting occupational safety and Process Safety Management initiatives. The role supports four manufacturing units and a wastewater treatment operation, partnering closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, and regulatory agencies to ensure compliance with air, water, waste, and chemical management requirements and maintain the site's license to operate.

Be part of a collaborative, safety-focused, solution-oriented, and growth-oriented
team where together we can achieve greatness and make a real impact.

Your potential is our inspiration.

The Memphis, Tennessee facility has an exciting opportunity for an Environmental Health & Safety Specialist
. This role supports environmental, health, and safety compliance and performance across the Memphis site, including four manufacturing units and a wastewater pH treatment facility. The Health & Safety Specialist helps manage environmental and operational risks while supporting the site's commitment to maintaining regulatory compliance and its license to operate.

This position serves as a key resource for interpreting regulations, implementing compliance programs, supporting continuous improvement initiatives, and partnering with operations and leadership teams to strengthen environmental, health, and safety performance.

The role collaborates with both local and corporate teams to ensure management systems remain effective and support the continued growth of the site.

Where You'll Make a Difference

Serve as a key environmental compliance resource for the site, providing technical guidance and ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Own and support environmental permitting and compliance programs, including air permits, wastewater permits, hazardous waste management, stormwater compliance, chemical reporting, permit renewals, and regulatory submissions.
Prepare, review, and submit environmental reports and compliance documentation while maintaining strong relationships with regulatory agencies and supporting environmental inspections and audits.
Lead environmental compliance assessments, identify risks and compliance gaps, and implement corrective and preventive actions to maintain the site's license to operate.
Partner with Operations, Engineering, and Maintenance teams to evaluate process changes, capital projects, and Management of Change activities for environmental compliance impacts.
Support the site's commitment to achieving zero occupational injuries and illnesses through proactive risk identification, hazard reduction, and prevention initiatives.
Provide leadership and support for Process Safety Management programs, including Management of Change, Process Hazard Analysis, and risk assessments.
Lead or participate in investigations of environmental incidents, permit exceedances, near misses, workplace injuries, and compliance events utilizing Root Cause Analysis methodologies.
Develop and deliver environmental, health, and safety training programs while preparing procedures, standards, and compliance documentation that strengthen site environmental stewardship and safety culture.

What Makes You The Right Fit

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Safety, Occupational Health, or a related discipline with at least two years of Environmental Health & Safety experience.
Alternatively, a minimum of five years of relevant Environmental Health & Safety experience in a manufacturing, industrial, chemical, food, or operations environment.
Hands-on experience managing environmental compliance programs within a manufacturing, chemical, food, industrial, or wastewater treatment environment.
Experience with environmental permitting, permit interpretation, permit renewals, regulatory reporting, inspections, compliance audits, and agency interactions related to air emissions, wastewater, hazardous waste, stormwater, or chemical management programs.
Strong understanding of Occupational Safety and Health Administration regulations and safe work practices, including confined space entry, line breaking, lockout/tagout, respiratory protection, contractor safety, and occupational safety programs.
Experience conducting environmental and safety audits, inspections, risk assessments, incident investigations, and compliance evaluations.
Ability to collaborate effectively across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Technology, Quality, Training, Research and Development, and corporate functions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to prepare regulatory reports, develop procedures, deliver training, and interact effectively with regulatory agencies.
Ability to analyze environmental performance data, compliance metrics, monitoring results, and operational trends to identify risks, implement corrective actions, and support continuous improvement initiatives.

How Would You Stand Out?

Experience serving as the environmental lead for a manufacturing or chemical facility, including ownership of air, wastewater, hazardous waste, and stormwater compliance programs.
Experience managing environmental permits, permit modifications, agency inspections, environmental reporting, Title V air programs, wastewater treatment systems, Toxic Release Inventory reporting, or Resource Conservation and Recovery Act compliance activities.
Professional certifications such as Certified Hazardous Materials Manager, Certified Industrial Hygienist, Certified Safety Professional, Professional Engineer, or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt.

Why Choose Us?

Opportunity to support a large-scale manufacturing operation with diverse environmental, health, and safety challenges.
Exposure to environmental compliance, occupational health, and Process Safety Management programs in a highly regulated environment.
Collaborative and inclusive culture focused on safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Professional development opportunities, including certification and leadership growth.
Access to a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k)
Opportunity to make a direct impact on employee safety, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.

The Food Ingredient business unit will remain part of IFF until close and, at such time, will transition to CVC Capital Partners. added.title: Chemical Regulatory Compliance Specialist 2
added.description:
L-H Battery Company, Inc., located in Jeffersonville, Ohio, is a Joint venture of LG Energy Solution and Honda to manufacture large lithium-ion polymer batteries. Products from L-H Battery power a variety of innovative energy storage applications.

Established in 2023, L-H Battery is passionate about developing and maintaining a culture where our associates and customers understand their value and worth. We are making a positive impact, and we want you to be a part of it!

Summary

Responsible for the day-to-day administration and oversight of the site's Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) compliance program. The role evaluates chemicals, mixtures, articles, raw materials, components, and process changes for applicable TSCA requirements before import, purchase, manufacture, processing, use, distribution, or disposition. The Specialist maintains defensible compliance records, coordinates cross-functional controls, monitors regulatory changes, supports reporting and notifications, and helps ensure that regulated substances and articles are managed in accordance with applicable federal requirements and company procedures.

Key Responsibilities

Administer the site's TSCA compliance program and maintain procedures, work instructions, decision records, and compliance calendars for applicable TSCA obligations.
Review new chemicals, mixtures, raw materials, battery materials, components, articles, and process changes before procurement, import, manufacture, processing, use, distribution, recycling, transfer, or disposal.
Confirm chemical identities and regulatory status using supplier documentation, Safety Data Sheets, Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) numbers, composition data, and applicable EPA resources; document inventory, exemption, exclusion, and article determinations.
Evaluate whether planned activities may require review under TSCA Section 5, including premanufacture, significant new use, low-volume, research-and-development, polymer, or other applicable new-chemical requirements.
Track site-specific manufacture and import volumes and coordinate data collection, applicability reviews, quality checks, and submissions for Chemical Data Reporting and other applicable TSCA reporting obligations.
Assess and implement applicable TSCA Section 6 risk-management requirements, restrictions, prohibitions, recordkeeping, labeling, downstream notification, and workplace chemical protection measures in coordination with Industrial Hygiene, Safety, Operations, and Legal.
Maintain a controlled TSCA chemical and article inventory with regulatory status, use, location, supplier, annual volume, import/export activity, applicable restrictions, approval status, and supporting documentation.
Establish and maintain a chemical/change-review workflow so TSCA approval is completed before introducing a new material, supplier, formulation, process, use, import route, product, recycle outlet, or disposition method.
Perform routine program audits and field verifications; document findings, assign corrective actions, conduct root-cause analysis, and verify timely closure and sustained countermeasures.
Monitor federal TSCA regulatory developments and EPA risk-management actions; assess site impact, communicate changes, and lead implementation plans with accountable owners and deadlines.
Develop and deliver role-based TSCA training for Procurement, Logistics, Engineering, Production, Quality, Environmental, Safety, and other employees whose work can affect chemical compliance.
Prepare accurate metrics and management updates covering chemical reviews, approval cycle time, open data gaps, import certifications, reporting status, audits, corrective actions, regulatory changes, and compliance risks.
Support agency inspections, information requests, internal reviews, and legal evaluations by organizing records, explaining program controls, and coordinating timely responses through Environmental leadership.
Serve as the technical TSCA point of contact for cross-functional projects while maintaining clear role boundaries with Waste, Dangerous Goods, Product Stewardship, Industrial Hygiene, and Legal functions.

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, or a science-related degree or equivalent related experience
3-6+ years of environmental experience

Knowledge/Skills

Experience using Microsoft Office products
Effective communication and presentation skills
Ability to manage and lead projects
Ability to work well in a collaborative environment
Effective planning and prioritization skills
Reliable and flexible
Strong data analysis and problem-solving skills
Ability to work effectively with contractors and production associates
General knowledge of environmental compliance requirements
Some understanding of business plans, budgeting, and cost reporting
Ability to support root cause analysis and implement countermeasures

What differentiates L-H Battery and makes us an employer of choice?

Ability to earn compensatory time off

Whether you're modernizing aging infrastructure or pioneering next-generation transportation solutions, your contributions will help define the future of mobility. We are all employee-owners at HDR, which is the foundation of our collaborative culture that connects employees around the world.

Primary Responsibilities

In the role of Senior Environmental Scientist/Project Manager, we'll count on you to

Plan and direct medium- to large-size environmental planning and compliance projects for transportation, facilities, and other programs as identified

Manage or coordinate specialty sub consultants or consultant team members
Define the level of environmental analysis required, coordinate with project team members in problem solving and solutions
Assist in preparation for and participation in public information meetings and hearings
Accomplish work independently and through coordinating or supervising small to large technical and professional teams from local and regional offices
Support regional or national projects in specific areas of technical expertise
Be closely involved in public participation and multiple agency coordination (specifically New England state DOT’s)
Take responsibility for project management, including developing and managing budgets, schedules, and quality of products
Serve as Project Manager or Task Leader on larger projects as needed, but project management is not the sole focus of position
Assist with business development/marketing for environmental services
Perform other duties as needed

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in environmental sciences or closely related field
PMP certification
Previous experience in the A/E industry desired
Preference is given to local candidates

Bachelor's degree in Environment Science or closely related field
10 years experience in complex environmental planning/compliance projects
Demonstrated knowledge of the NEPA process
Experience managing large, complex EIS documents for transportation, large facility, land management, or other infrastructure projects
Technical expertise in the design, implementation, interpretation and presentation of data for environmental studies and investigations in specialized discipline
Proficient with MS Office
Self-starter with excellent writing and communication skills
Strong conceptual, organizational, problem-solving and research abilities
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Staff management experience beneficial
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

added.description:
About Us

Groundbreaker. Game changer. Pioneer.

TRC has consistently set the standard for clients needing more than just engineering services by blending scientific expertise with cutting-edge technology to create innovative, enduring solutions. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

Our team works with a diverse range of commercial, industrial and government clients and the communities they serve. We are dedicated to delivering creative solutions that meet local needs, helping our clients thrive in a rapidly changing world. Together, we tackle challenges and strive to make the Earth a better place to live, community by community and project by project.

Joining TRC means engaging in interesting, meaningful projects. We pride ourselves on our collaborative spirit, entrepreneurial zeal and agile corporate structure. We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications. At TRC, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where every team member can thrive. We offer a range of People Programs designed to support our employees' growth and well-being. Explore our programs here: TRC People Programs

At TRC, every voice is valued, every individual has the opportunity to make a difference, and together we shape a brighter, more sustainable future.

Overview

TRC is seeking an Environmental Scientist/Industrial Hygiene Inspector to join our Windsor, CT Office. This position would be working within our Building Sciences and Industrial Hygiene business within our Environmental Sector.

Responsibilities

Perform hazardous building material inspections for asbestos, lead-based paint, PCBs.
Perform indoor air quality inspections, water intrusion investigation and mold assessments.
Perform project oversight and coordination with contractors.
Operate and maintain instruments including sampling pumps, calibrators and microscopes.
Collect samples as required by various regulatory agencies, complete data sheets, mobile data apps, chain of custody forms, and prepare samples for shipment to laboratory.
Maintain daily logs of activities related to project work.
Interact and communicate with clients, contractors and regulatory agency representatives.
Read project specifications and drawings.
Prepare reports.
Travel throughout Connecticut expected.
